title: Night IR camera-trap training subset (LILA BC)
description: 2714 night infrared (monochrome) frames from fixed outdoor camera traps at 462 camera locations, 926 MB (925830552 bytes): images with 520 deer, 520 opossum, 520 skunk, 520 fox, 111 raccoon, 106 bird, 12 cat, 9 squirrel, 5 dog, 1 car (2421 boxes), and 407 empty frames (15%, hard negatives). Sources: Caltech Camera Traps (764) and WCS Camera Traps (1059) by capture time 20:00-05:00, Channel Islands Camera Traps (890; no capture times) and NACTI vehicle frames (1; EXIF time where present) by a mean luma below 110 when there is no time; every frame passes the grayscale (IR) test (chroma spread < 3.0/255). Every animal in a frame is boxed with one of these labels (species mapped: e.g. brocket deer and muntjac are deer, gray and culpeo foxes fox, wildcats cat): frames with other animals (coyote, bobcat, rabbit, rodent, peccary, ...) are left out. Disjoint from the nir-night benchmark set by image and by camera location (none of its cameras is used; ENA24, which has no camera ids, is left out entirely). Not reviewed by hand: the empty frames are those LILA labels empty, and LILA's empty labels are per sequence, so a few may hold a missed (often small or distant) animal. Labels are collect.classes names (vehicles are car); boxes are pixels [x_min, y_min, x_max, y_max].
